meta.title: Xnapper Case Study — Nahuel Uliassi Pirchio
meta.description: How I took Xnapper from a screenshot tool to a full video editing product — video pipeline, architecture, reliability and licensing, end to end.

header.summary: Over sixteen months, I worked across the product stack of Xnapper, taking ownership of complex editing, processing, persistence and reliability features for a commercial product used by approximately 20,000 active users.

paragraphs: Xnapper is a commercial screenshot tool that expanded into image and video editing. As a Software Developer on the team, I owned features across the interface, application state, processing, persistence and service integrations — not a single layer of the stack.

The technical difficulty came from moving beyond static screenshot editing into frame-accurate video workflows that had to stay reliable and maintainable across different runtime environments, without sacrificing performance.

challenge.statement: The product needed to move beyond static screenshot editing and support reliable video workflows without sacrificing performance, maintainability or consistency across environments.

built.title: Product state & architecture
bullets: Undo/redo history based on the Memento pattern

decisions.title: Demuxer-based frame extraction
decisions.problem: Native video seeking wasn't reliable on variable-frame-rate footage — a seek could land on the wrong frame, breaking frame-accurate editing.
decisions.approach: Extracted frames through a demuxer instead of relying on native seek, giving the editor a consistent, frame-accurate source regardless of a clip's original encoding.

decisions.title: Export strategies
decisions.problem: Supporting multiple export targets was spreading conditional logic across the codebase, making every new export option riskier to add.
decisions.approach: Introduced a shared export strategy interface so each target implements the same contract, keeping the branching logic in one place instead of scattered conditionals.

decisions.title: Persistent undo history
decisions.problem: As the editor grew new capabilities, ad-hoc undo handling meant each feature had to reinvent its own way of tracking and reverting state.
decisions.approach: Modeled undo/redo as state snapshots, a Memento-style approach, so any new editor capability could plug into the same history mechanism without custom undo logic.

items: Expanded the product from screenshot-focused workflows into video editing.
Shipped the work through multiple production releases.
Improved maintainability of export and persistence flows.
Reduced important security and reliability risks.
Supported a product used by approximately 20,000 active users.
